github_action_pinning_note: Every external action is pinned to a full immutable commit SHA; a tag can be moved, a commit SHA cannot. Tags are recorded for human readability only. Same actions, same SHAs as tools/hyp01_r_reference -- both bridges share one CI toolchain and there is no reason for these to differ.

observed_snapshot_binary_instability.what_was_observed: This bridge installed the identical package NAMES and VERSIONS as tools/hyp01_r_reference (verified with numeric_version(), not a string compare), from the identical dated CRAN snapshot URL (https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/2026-08-11). All 10 installed binaries were re-downloaded separately on 2026-09-10 to compute their own SHA-256, and EVERY one differs in both byte size and SHA-256 from the value recorded in tools/hyp01_r_reference/r-packages.lock.json for the same (package, version) pair.
observed_snapshot_binary_instability.example: clubSandwich 0.7.0: HYP-01 recorded 657114 bytes / sha256 3506c23e646d328f4d870076df956948395b018c3ea920d0181e20d42ab1482a. This bridge measured 656607 bytes / sha256 042c62495aa24cc8ab57345c8aa67f2d2e295365d23285c11940fe7115538292, fetched from the SAME snapshot URL roughly one month later.
observed_snapshot_binary_instability.not_claimed: No explanation for the byte difference is asserted here -- it was not investigated beyond confirming the version string and package name are unchanged. It could be repackaging on the snapshot server, a compression/metadata difference, or something else; this file does not guess.
observed_snapshot_binary_instability.what_this_does_and_does_not_affect: Version pinning is UNAFFECTED and still holds exactly (verified below). Byte-level local authentication is affected: the SHA-256 values in THIS file authenticate only what was actually downloaded onto THIS workstation on 2026-09-10, not tools/hyp01_r_reference's recorded values, and the two must not be assumed interchangeable.
observed_snapshot_binary_instability.relevance_beyond_hyp04: This observation was made in the course of building this bridge, not as a scheduled audit of tools/hyp01_r_reference. It is recorded here because it is what this bridge's own install actually showed; it is not a corrective edit to any other hypothesis's already-committed lockfile.

pinning_model.ci_linux: Pinned by (dated CRAN snapshot + exact version). CI installs from the snapshot below and then verifies the INSTALLED version of every package in this file against `version`, failing closed on any absence or difference. A Windows binary SHA-256 is NOT used, and does not authenticate, the Linux installation.
pinning_model.local_windows: Pinned by (version + SHA-256 of the CRAN Windows binary actually downloaded to this workstation on 2026-09-10). Those hashes are platform- AND download-time-specific -- see observed_snapshot_binary_instability above -- and authenticate only this install, not any other download of the same (name, version) from the same URL.
pinning_model.not_claimed: This lockfile does not claim byte-level authentication of the Linux packages, and -- per observed_snapshot_binary_instability -- does not claim the recorded Windows binary hashes are stable across time even from the identical snapshot URL. It claims exact version pinning, enforced by a CI check over every package listed here, and verified locally with numeric_version() on 2026-09-10.

purpose: Pinned R runtime and package versions for HYP-04's D10 independent CR2/Satterthwaite reference. Installing these approves no statistical method.

r.installer_sha256_note: Identical to tools/hyp01_r_reference's recorded value -- verified by direct comparison on 2026-09-10. Unlike the CRAN package binaries above, the R installer itself DID reproduce byte-for-byte.

sources.ci_snapshot_note: Same dated snapshot URL as tools/hyp01_r_reference, reused deliberately so CI resolves the identical package VERSIONS for both bridges -- not a claim that it resolves identical BYTES; see observed_snapshot_binary_instability.
